source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Pomelo fruit is ready for harvest a few years after planting, once fruit reaches full size and the characteristic flavor and juice content for the variety have developed; the source notes that from planting, pomelo can begin producing marketable fruit within about 2-3 years for marcotted/grafted trees.

Fruit should be cut from the tree rather than pulled, leaving a short stem attached, to avoid tearing the skin at the stem end (a common entry point for stem-end rot after harvest - see the Melanose/Stem-End Rot entry). Harvested fruit is sorted by size and quality before sale, since larger, blemish-free pomelo commands a higher price.
